heading: How we handle your data
intro: Your data is yours, and we build so it stays that way — much of the work never touches your real data at all.

sections.heading: Sample-first by default
sections.body: Most of an automation is structure — how something is read, sorted, and drafted. That part can be built and tested against samples or made-up examples, often with no real data of yours involved at all.

sections.heading: Real data — only to test, only before handover
sections.body: When it's time to prove the automation works end to end, we may need to use your real data. That happens in a defined, limited window before handover: used only to test, then cleared. It is never kept beyond that work, and never shared.

sections.heading: Live — in your systems
sections.body: Once it's running, the automation works in or alongside your own systems. We only ever touch what a given task needs.

sections.heading: What we never do
sections.body: Keep your data beyond the work | Share it with anyone | Use it for anything other than the job you asked for

sections.heading: What an AI service sees
sections.body: You decide what, if anything, an outside AI service is ever shown. Sensitive work — finance, legal, health — is handled with stricter limits on what leaves your environment.

sections.heading: A person approves every step
sections.body: Nothing is sent, paid, or filed on its own. That human step isn't only reassurance — it's also what the rules below expect of automated decisions that affect people.

sections.heading: The rules we work to
sections.body: revDSG — Switzerland's data-protection law, in force since September 2023. It sets how personal data must be handled: used only for a clear purpose, kept secure, not kept longer than needed, and open to the person it concerns. | GDPR — the EU's equivalent. It applies when a business serves or monitors people in the EU. Because we work with clients worldwide, we build to both. | Both expect a human in the loop for automated decisions that significantly affect someone — a review a person can ask for. Our approve-every-step design is that review, built in.

sections.heading: Working together
sections.body: When we handle data on your behalf, we sign a data-processing agreement — you as the controller, us as the processor — that puts all of this in writing. Ask us for it any time.
This page describes how we work; it isn't legal advice. For your own obligations, your lawyer or fiduciary is the right guide.
